topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the final course lecture by introducing the topic of cancer therapy and stating the intended learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss standard cancer therapies, focusing on surgical excision, radiation-induced DNA damage, cytotoxic drug mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and efflux-pump resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities and Genetic Defects in Cancer Cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how therapies can exploit cancer cell-specific weaknesses, such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, oncolytic viral vulnerability, and DNA repair deficiencies via synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction, Kinase Inhibitors, and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the development and application of small-molecule inhibitors against oncogenic kinases, alongside the mechanisms of acquired drug resistance, bypass signaling, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibody Therapies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on using engineered monoclonal antibodies to target surface antigens, mediate immune cytotoxicity, and deliver linked cytotoxic payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell-Directed Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis for tumor immunity and examine advanced cellular immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibition, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review overall progress in cancer survival, outlining systemic hurdles in trial design and tumor heterogeneity as well as future considerations in early detection, biomarkers, and treatment ethics.
